questions.q: What specifically makes governing Microsoft Fabric different from general data governance theory, per this lesson?
options: Fabric has no governance features at all, so none of the theory applies
Every workload shares one tenant-wide lake, so a mistake isn't boxed into one tool â€” it's visible tenant-wide by default
Fabric only supports a single user per tenant
Governance only matters for the Power BI workload, not the others
questions.explain: Because every Fabric workload stores its data in the same OneLake under one tenant, a permission mistake or ungoverned workspace isn't isolated to one product the way it might be across separate disconnected tools.

questions.q: How do you reach the Fabric admin portal?
options: The gear icon in the top right of Fabric, then Admin portal
Typing /admin into the workspace search bar
A link inside every lakehouse's "..." menu
Signing in to a separate admin.fabric.microsoft.com site
questions.explain: The admin portal is reached from the gear icon (top right of the Fabric interface) and then Admin portal â€” a separate surface from the everyday workspace view.

questions.q: What does a Fabric domain group workspaces by?
options: Business area (like Finance or Health), for org-wide discovery and governance
Compute capacity and region, the same way a capacity does
Alphabetical order of workspace name
The Microsoft Entra ID tenant they belong to
questions.explain: A domain groups workspaces by business area â€” distinct from a workspace's own permissions and from a capacity, which groups by compute and region rather than business meaning.

questions.q: What is a Fabric workspace?
options: The fundamental container every Fabric item â€” lakehouse, warehouse, report, pipeline â€” lives inside
A folder used only to organize items after they've already been deployed
A single Power BI report and nothing else
A synonym for a Microsoft Entra ID tenant
questions.explain: The workspace is Fabric's fundamental container and the real unit of deployment â€” every item lives inside exactly one workspace, which also determines who can see and edit it.

questions.q: What is OneLake?
options: One automatic, tenant-wide data lake underlying every Fabric workspace â€” not something provisioned per project
A separate lake a team must manually create for each new workspace
A Power BI feature unrelated to Lakehouses or Warehouses
A synonym for a Fabric capacity
questions.explain: OneLake exists the moment the Fabric tenant does and every workspace draws from it â€” nobody provisions a separate lake per project the way you might spin up a new storage account.

questions.q: What is the core structural difference between a Lakehouse and a Warehouse in Fabric?
options: A Lakehouse is schema-on-read and flexible; a Warehouse is a T-SQL engine that enforces a defined schema
A Lakehouse only stores files; a Warehouse only stores tables
A Warehouse cannot be queried with SQL at all
There is no structural difference â€” they are the same item type under a different name
questions.explain: A Lakehouse stores files and tables together and applies structure at query time (schema-on-read). A Warehouse is a full T-SQL engine with an enforced, defined schema (schema-on-write).

questions.q: How does OneLake security differ from a workspace role?
options: OneLake security is item-level, controlling which rows and columns are visible; a workspace role only gates access to the item itself
OneLake security and workspace roles are two names for exactly the same setting
OneLake security replaces workspace roles entirely â€” workspace roles no longer matter once it's enabled
OneLake security only applies to Power BI reports, never to lakehouses or warehouses
questions.explain: Workspace roles (Lesson 5) gate access to the Fabric item itself. OneLake security is a finer-grained layer inside the item that controls exactly which rows and columns a role's members can see.

questions.q: What is a OneLake shortcut, per this lesson?
options: A reference inside a Lakehouse that points at data living elsewhere, without physically copying it
A keyboard shortcut for navigating the Fabric admin portal
A compressed backup copy of a table
A deprecated feature replaced by OneLake Catalog
questions.explain: A shortcut looks like a normal folder inside the Lakehouse, but every read resolves through to the real, external location.

questions.q: What specific gap do OneLake data access roles close that workspace roles can't?
options: Granting access to only specific folders or tables inside one Lakehouse, instead of the whole item
Letting a Viewer become a Workspace Admin
Encrypting data in transit between Fabric and the client
Replacing the need for Microsoft Entra ID authentication
questions.explain: Workspace roles like Contributor or Viewer apply to an entire item or workspace; data access roles scope read (or read/write) access down to specific checked tables and folders within one Lakehouse.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Fabric workspace role and an item permission?
options: A workspace role applies to everything in the workspace; an item permission is confined to a single item
Workspace roles only exist for Admins; item permissions are for everyone else
Item permissions override workspace roles entirely
There is no difference â€” they are two names for the same thing
questions.explain: Workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) apply to every item in that workspace. Item permissions are granted on one item at a time, independent of any workspace role.

questions.q: What is a sensitivity label in Fabric and Power BI?
options: A Microsoft Purview classification tag (e.g. Public, General, Confidential, Highly Confidential) that carries its own protection settings
A workspace role that controls which items a user can open
A DAX filter expression that restricts which rows a user sees
A tag that only exists inside Power BI and has no relationship to Office or email
questions.explain: A sensitivity label is Microsoft Purview Information Protection's classification tag, applied to Fabric items, and it reuses the same labels used for Office documents and email.

questions.q: Where do you actually search Fabric's audit log?
options: The Microsoft Purview portal, searching the unified audit log
A dedicated 'Audit' screen inside the Fabric workspace itself
The Power BI Desktop application's File menu
The OneLake catalog
questions.explain: Fabric auditing is a setting turned on in the admin portal, but the actual search happens in the Microsoft Purview portal's unified audit log â€” the same log every other Microsoft 365 workload writes to.

questions.q: What does the global Search box at the top of the Fabric portal search by?
options: Item name, title, creator, tag, or workspace, across every workspace you have access to
Only item names within your currently open workspace
Only the names of Fabric administrators
Only items that have been Certified
questions.explain: Global search finds items by name, title, creator, tag, or workspace across the whole tenant, powered by Azure AI Search, and results are trimmed to what you're allowed to see.

questions.q: Where do you open the OneLake catalog in Microsoft Fabric?
options: From the OneLake catalog icon in the Fabric navigation pane
Only from the Admin portal
Only from inside a workspace's settings menu
From a separate standalone application outside Fabric
questions.explain: The OneLake catalog is opened from its own icon in the Fabric left navigation pane, and the same catalog is also embedded in Teams, Excel, and Copilot Studio.

questions.q: Where does Fabric's lineage view come from, and what setup does it require?
options: Every workspace has one automatically, with no extra setup or licensing
It must be manually enabled per workspace by an admin
It only exists after you connect a dataflow to a semantic model
It requires a separate Purview subscription to activate
questions.explain: Every workspace automatically has a lineage view â€” it's built in, not something you turn on.

questions.q: How does impact analysis differ from the lineage view covered in the previous lesson?
options: Lineage view maps how items connect; impact analysis quantifies which downstream items a planned change would affect, including items in other workspaces lineage view doesn't show
They are the exact same feature under two different names
Impact analysis only works on reports, while lineage view only works on lakehouses
Lineage view requires write permission, but impact analysis works for anyone with any access level
questions.explain: Lineage view shows structure within one workspace; impact analysis specifically sizes up the downstream blast radius of a change, reaching items and workspaces lineage view's one-workspace graph can't show.

questions.q: What does a semantic model's item page show, per this lesson?
options: An owner, an inherited sensitivity label, and tabs for Overview, Lineage, Monitor, and Permissions â€” the same governance surface any Fabric item carries
Only the DAX formulas used in its measures, with no owner or label information
Nothing â€” semantic models have no item page of their own
A list of every report ever built from the model, with no other metadata
questions.explain: A semantic model is a Fabric item in its own right, carrying the same owner/label/tabs governance surface as any other item.

questions.q: Per this lesson, how does endorsement differ from a workspace role or an item permission?
options: It's a signal flagging which self-service items are worth building on, not a gate controlling who can access something
It is functionally identical to a workspace role, just with a different name
It replaces the need for any item permissions entirely
It only applies to items nobody has permission to view
questions.explain: Roles and permissions are gates deciding access; endorsement is a separate signal pointing people at the items worth using.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does an organization running Fabric alongside other platforms still need Microsoft Purview's catalog?
options: Because the OneLake catalog is scoped to Fabric â€” non-Fabric sources like a SQL Server or Snowflake account never show up in it
Because the OneLake catalog has been fully replaced by Purview and no longer functions
Because Purview and the OneLake catalog contain identical information with no difference at all
Because Fabric items cannot be governed at all without Purview
questions.explain: Purview is Microsoft's enterprise-wide catalog, spanning both Fabric and non-Fabric sources â€” the OneLake catalog only covers the Fabric estate.

questions.q: Is Northfield Health Network, the organization in this case study, a real healthcare system?
options: No â€” it's explicitly described as a fictional, illustrative composite scenario
Yes â€” it is a real, named regional healthcare system
Yes â€” it is real, but with its name changed for privacy
The lesson does not say whether it is real or fictional
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels Northfield Health Network as fictional and illustrative, not a real organization, consistent with this catalog's policy against presenting invented scenarios as real.
